title: Registered Bioimaging of Nanomaterials for Diagnostic and Therapeutic Monitoring
protocol: Measure the size, charge, and shape of the SPIO model system.
Determine the cytotoxicity of the SPIO model system.
Incubate cells with the candidate SPIO model nanoformulation to determine relaxivity within the cells.
Prepare phantoms composed of labeled cells suspended in agar gel.
Prepare phantoms in triplicate at various concentrations.
Quantify the relaxivity due to SPIO uptake in cells using phantoms.
Determine if the nanoformulations affect the oxidation state of SPIO.
Assess the visibility of SPIO in MRI scans.
Prepare catheters using a non-magnetic needle and tubing extension with minimum diameter.
Prefill catheters with either the solution containing the nanomaterial or saline.
If possible, follow injection with a physiological saline flush.
Perform pre-scan to determine predetermined time for injection before scans.
Insert catheter into the tail vein for I.V. injections.
Place animal in a chamber filled with 1.5% isoflurane in 70% nitrous oxide and 30% oxygen.
Ensure animal is fully anesthetized before removing from chamber.
Transfer anesthetized animal to stereotactic holder equipped with breath rate and temperature monitors.
Continue supplying isoflurane during set-up and scanning.
Set up eye lubricant to protect against corneal ulcers in the animal holder setup.
Lightly wrap the animal with gauze and tape it to minimize heat loss during scanning and provide positive pressure against the breathing monitor.
Adjust tooth bars on the animal holder for vertical and horizontal alignment of the head.
Ensure proper positioning of the head angle in the caudal-rostral direction.
Avoid rotations of the head as much as feasible to maintain magnetic field homogeneity.
Allow rotation compensation by adjusting the animal holder within the magnet.
Place the head carefully prior to inserting the animal into the MRI system.
Determine the initial position of the animal in the scanner.
Take a 3-plane localizer image to determine the precise position of the animal.
Adjust the homogeneity of the magnetic field by mapping the field distribution.
Calculate spatial corrections based on responses of shim coils within the system.
Use a multi-gradient echo sequence and mapping software for shimming.
Match regions of homogeneity to the region examined by each imaging method.
Acquire the scan(s) of interest from the animal.
Determine the biodistribution of SPIO containing nanoparticles using high resolution T2* weighted MRI.
Acquire localizer scans to determine the region of the brain for analysis.
Acquire a T2* weighted MRI scan with 150 micron isotropic resolution.
Use a 25 mm birdcage volume coil for acquisition parameters including echo time = 5 ms, repetition time = 50 ms, 30% echo, flip angle = 35 degrees, averages = 2, field of view = 20 x 20 x 20 mm.
Acquire a high resolution 3D gradient recalled echo MRI scan with a resolution of 128 x 128 x 128 (voxel size = 150 x 150 x 150 μm³).
Employ respiratory gated spin-echo diffusion weighted echo planar imaging (EPI) MR sequence for DTI acquisition.
Shim the scanned region carefully.
Ensure off-resonance effects during signal evolution are minimized.
Acquire EPI images with 14 slices and a bandwidth of 200 KHz.
Use a 96 x 96 in-plane acquisition, zero-filled to 256 x 256.
Set the slice thickness to 0.5 mm for EPI scans.
Apply a balanced, rotationally-invariant diffusion encoding scheme (12 directions).
Design the encoding scheme to reduce background-diffusion gradient couplings.
Use a b-factor of 800 s mm-2 with δ=4 ms and Δ=15 ms.
Set Gdmax to 40 G/cm with a rise time of 200 μs.
Acquire 7 averages for the b=0 scan direction.
Collect 3 averages for each of the 12 b=800 encoding directions.
Complete the acquisition in approximately 20-40 minutes, depending on respiration rate.
Identify anatomical locations on images to prescribe the region of interest for MRS.
Perform shimming on a region matching the volume of acquisition using a localized water spectrum.
Optimize the power of water suppression pulses.
Measure water frequency to ensure it is on resonance.
Acquire a short test spectrum for quality control.
Check system settings, including RF power and shim settings, if spectra are of insufficient quality.
Run a second 3-plane localizer if the animal has moved from initial scans.
Acquire spectra in short blocks with resetting of the system frequency between acquisitions.
Use a single pulse water spectrum at predefined preamplifier gain as a quantitative signal amplitude reference.
Perfuse the mouse after the final MRI scanning session.
Remove and embed the brain into an OCT block darkened using India ink.
Place the OCT block into a cryostat for slicing and histological analysis.
Acquire blockface images every 50 micrometers through the entire brain volume.
Align individual blockface slices to reconstruct the 3D volume using the block outlines in Analyze software package.
Automatically segment the brain volume using seed based region growing algorithm in AnalyzeDirect software.
